signal.title: Energy-Structured Latent World Models with Neural Time Fields for Physically Constistent Open-World Motion Planning
signal.summary: 这篇论文针对具身智能中的一个核心难题：世界模型预测出的未来轨迹，必须符合真实物理，而不能只在视觉上看起来合理。作者提出能量结构化潜在世界模型，把能量和动量显式放进潜在状态，并将其接入基于物理的神经时间场，用于开放世界运动规划。

editorial.intro: 这篇论文针对具身智能中的一个核心难题：世界模型预测出的未来轨迹，必须符合真实物理，而不能只在视觉上看起来合理。作者提出能量结构化潜在世界模型，把能量和动量显式放进潜在状态，并将其接入基于物理的神经时间场，用于开放世界运动规划。
editorial.why_it_matters: 它把世界模型从“预测未来”推进到“预测可执行的未来”：如果结果能在更多场景中复现，可能改善机器人导航的安全性、碰撞控制和运动规划可靠性。
editorial.watch_next: 继续核对完整论文实验、代码或模型是否开放，以及在真实机器人上的验证。

evidence.title: Energy-Structured Latent World Models with Neural Time Fields for Physically Constistent Open-World Motion Planning
evidence.excerpt: Physically consistent motion planning remains a fundamental challenge in embodied AI, as generated trajectories must strictly conform to real-world execution dynamics. While latent world models offer a promising approach by predicting these dynamics, existing methods learn unconstrained future representations where absorbed physics remains implicit. Therefore, they fail to form reusable physical knowledge, which compromises reliability in unpredictable open-world navigation. To address this, we propose a novel Energy-Structured Latent World Model (ELWM). Our key idea is to structure the ELWM latent state to explicitly carry energy and momentum, ensuring strictly causal transitions via dissipation and control ports. Trained on multimodal RGB-D and inertial interaction histories, our model guarantees physically consistent predictions. We further implement this for motion planning by constructing Physics-Conditioned Neural Time Fields (PC-NTF), a key technical cornerstone that integrates ELWM into an arrival time field via the Eikonal equation to yield a physically-informed navigation policy.
